title: Change in Body Weight During Treatment of Advanced Colorectal Cancer
brief_summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a significant and growing health burden in Hong Kong. According to data from Hong Kong Cancer Registry, CRC ranked the first in incidence and the second in mortality, with around 5,000 new cases diagnosed and more than 2,000 cancer-related mortality in 2014. The investigators aim to evaluate the association between serial weight change during first line treatment and outcomes in patients with metastatic CRC.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of colorectal origin
* Stage IV disease with systemic treatment
* Estimated life expectancy \>3 months
* Adequate organ functions

Exclusion Criteria:

* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 3 or above
* Pregnancy
* Human immunodeficiency virus infection and acquired immune deficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS)
* Past medical history of another cancer
study_population: Single institutional cohort of stage IV (advanced) colorectal cancer patients who undergo systemic treatments.
